grammar.label: free indirect speech — a character's voice inside the narrator's
grammar.form: third person and past tense of narration, with the vocabulary and stance of the character
grammar.meaning: reports a thought without quoting it or announcing it

explanation.en: 'She would not go. The whole thing was absurd — had been absurd from the start.' No quotation marks, no 'she thought', yet the judgement is hers, not the narrator's. The markers are the character's own words and rhythm carried in the narrator's tense and person. Reading it as the narrator's own view is the commonest misreading in fiction.
explanation.uz: 'She would not go. The whole thing was absurd.' Qo'shtirnoq ham, 'she thought' ham yo'q, lekin baho — qahramonniki. Belgilar: qahramonning so'zlari va ohangi, lekin hikoyachining zamoni va shaxsida.

grammar.positive_example: He checked the file again. Twice in one week — and still nobody had signed it.
grammar.negative_example: He checked the file again. He thought that it was twice in one week and that nobody had signed it.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek adabiyotida ichki nutq ko'pincha aniq belgilanadi; belgilanmagan shakl tanish emas.

grammar.label: genre at C1 — the review, the obituary and the leading article
grammar.form: conventional section order, tense and stance for each genre
grammar.meaning: meets the expectations a reader brings to a kind of text

explanation.en: A review describes in the present, judges in the present, and gives its verdict early or holds it for the last line — both are conventional, and drifting between them is not. An obituary opens with the death and the claim to significance, then runs chronologically. A leading article states a position, concedes the strongest objection, and ends with what should be done.
explanation.uz: Taqriz hozirgi zamonda tasvirlaydi va baholaydi. Nekrolog o'lim va ahamiyat bilan boshlanadi, so'ng xronologik davom etadi. Bosh maqola pozitsiyani bayon qiladi, eng kuchli e'tirozni tan oladi va nima qilish kerakligi bilan tugaydi.

grammar.positive_example: The novel is at its best in the middle third; the ending, sadly, is not earned.
grammar.negative_example: The novel was at its best in the middle third; the ending is not earned, sadly it was.

l1_notes.uz: Janr konventsiyalari madaniyatga bog'liq; ingliz matbuotidagi shakl o'zbek an'anasidan farq qiladi.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: The report went to the ministry on Friday. What now?

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Kamola asked me to write about Karimova's book for the teachers' journal.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: A review, then. Different rules entirely.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I have written the first line four times.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: 'The book is at its best in the middle third; the ending is not earned.'

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Present tense, judgement early, and you have said something a reader can disagree with. That is a review.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: I wrote the first three in the past tense.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Which would be a summary of a book that no longer exists. The book is still arguing.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: There is a passage I cannot place. 'He checked the file again. Twice in one week — and still nobody had signed it.'

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Whose judgement is 'twice in one week'?

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: And there is no 'he thought' anywhere. That is the whole trick, and half her readers take it for the narrator's own voice.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Mr Karimov retires in March. Kamola wants me to write something for that too.

body.speaker: Sarah
body.text: Then you will have written a report, a review and an obituary in one year, and each one to a different shape. He taught you the first. You worked out the other two yourself.
